### CHEOPS M-dwarf flares, against Poyatos et al. 2025 (aggregate only; gated)

Data: CHEOPS DRP (subarray) light curves via DACE public mode; Poyatos et al. used 3-s imagettes reduced with PIPE, which DACE does not serve. Targets and visits used: AU Mic 25 of 262 public; AD Leo 7 of 7 public; EV Lac 4 of 4 public; GJ 65 10 of 10 public; Proxima Cen 3 of 3 public.

**Gates.** Injected flares with S/N ≥ 10 and FWHM ≥ 3 cadences: 183/357 recovered [0.46, 0.56] (all injections: 454/1501). Flux-inverted null with the real flares masked: 7 (original) and 8 (denoised) against 47 and 57 flares (largest fraction 0.15). False splits of injected single flares: 46/422. The comparisons below count only if both gates pass.

**Where the injections landed.** Amplitude and FWHM are drawn once per injection (log-uniform, FWHM 0.5-10 min) and only the position is redrawn; a flare is placed when its start (one FWHM before the peak) and its peak plus three FWHM fall inside one stretch of data (cf. Poyatos et al. 2025, Sect. 2.3, who count only flares whose start and stop fall within one visit). Placed: 1501; no position found: 851.

| FWHM (min) | Placed | Placed fraction | Expected (log-uniform) |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0.50-0.91 | 418 | 0.28 | 0.20 |
| 0.91-1.66 | 378 | 0.25 | 0.20 |
| 1.66-3.02 | 292 | 0.19 | 0.20 |
| 3.02-5.49 | 226 | 0.15 | 0.20 |
| 5.49-10.00 | 187 | 0.12 | 0.20 |

| Quantity | SetuHQ original | SetuHQ denoised | Poyatos et al. 2025 (journal) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Flares | 47 in 11.29 d | 57 | 349 on 63 M dwarfs (imagettes) |
| Gain from denoising | | +21% | +34% |
| Complex fraction | 0.53 [0.39, 0.67] | 0.42 [0.3, 0.55] | ≈ 0.40 |
| Power-law α (above our median energy) | 2.20 ± 0.28 (n = 19) | 2.07 ± 0.22 (n = 23) | 1.92 ± 0.07 |
| Power law vs log-normal | R = -0.57, p = 0.49: neither (p ≥ 0.1) | R = -1.07, p = 0.32: neither (p ≥ 0.1) | log-normal preferred |

The arXiv v2 numbers differ (291 flares on 62 stars, ~42% complex, +35%, α = 1.99 ± 0.10); the journal version's are used. Without a CHEOPS completeness curve per star, the power law is fitted above the median energy, not above a 90% completeness energy as Poyatos et al. do; the indices are not strictly comparable. Energies use the TIC radius and, where the TIC has no Teff, the Teff from the CHEOPS archive (labelled).

### Detrending against pycheops (Maxted et al. 2022), same 15 decorrelation terms

| Visit | Programme | Points | Same input: rms difference (ppm), correlation | Same input: rms ours / pycheops (ppm) | End to end: rms difference, correlation | Raw inputs (DACE vs pycheops' DRP product) | End to end: rms ours / pycheops (ppm) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| CH_PR100018_TG035201_V0300 | CH_PR100018 | 135 | 0.03, 1.0000 | 2750 / 2750 | 1445, 0.886 | 1056, 0.9941 | 3111 / 2750 |
| CH_PR100018_TG048901_V0300 | CH_PR100018 | 227 | 685.66, 0.6863 | 648 / 1706 | 748, 0.612 | 160, 0.9993 | 583 / 1706 |
| CH_PR100018_TG049601_V0300 | CH_PR100018 | 255 | 0.52, 1.0000 | 17861 / 17861 | 14092, 0.763 | 105, 1.0000 | 21784 / 17861 |

On the same input, the linear decorrelation is the same model and gives the same light curve where both fits reach the least-squares optimum; where they differ, the one with the larger rms (on the same points and terms) is off the optimum. End to end, the inputs differ: pycheops reads the DRP FITS product and subtracts the contamination estimate, SetuHQ reads DACE's DRP arrays and keeps every unflagged point, so the detrended curves differ by about the difference of their inputs.

### HR 10, CHEOPS (public DRP visits)

Three visits together (22.2 d, 8152 points): 2 frequencies at S/N ≥ 4; f1, f2 found: [True, True]; 1.00 of ours match Salmon et al.'s TESS S29 list within 1/T, which recovers 0.03 of that list (0.20 of its 10 strongest). Background b: 101, 1727 µHz.

| Visit | Programme | Days | Frequencies (S/N ≥ 4) | f1, f2 found | Decorrelation terms |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| CH_PR100010_TG001501_V0300 | CH_PR100010 | 2.05 | 1 | [True, False] | sin2 |
| CH_PR100010_TG001502_V0300 | CH_PR100010 | 2.03 | 2 | [True, False] | t |
| CH_PR100010_TG001503_V0300 | CH_PR100010 | 2.06 | 2 | [True, True] | t, t2, cos2, cos1 |

Salmon et al. used PIPE photometry of the 3-s imagettes (67 ppm per minute); DACE serves the DRP subarray light curve (42 s). They publish no CHEOPS frequency list, so ours is compared with their TESS sector 29 list. Their CHEOPS granulation frequency (first visit): 165.06 µHz.
